entries.title: Pressure cusp and the order of thermodynamic and zero-field limits
entries.statement: Fix beta>0. For each N let M_N be symmetric in law with |M_N|<=N, and put p_N(h)=(beta N)^{-1}log E exp(beta h M_N). Suppose p_N(h) converges to a finite p(h) for every h in an open interval (-h0,h0). Then p is even, convex, 1-Lipschitz, p(0)=0, and for 0<2h<h0, p(h)/h <= liminf_N p_N'(h) <= limsup_N p_N'(h) <= [p(2h)-p(h)]/h. Both outer expressions tend to p'_+(0) as h decreases to zero, whereas p_N'(0)=0 for each N.
entries.proof_text: The bounded exponential moment is differentiable with p_N'(h)=E_h M_N/N, p_N''(h)=beta Var_h(M_N)/N>=0 and |p_N'|<=1. Symmetry makes p_N even and p_N'(0)=0. Convex secants give p_N(h)/h<=p_N'(h)<=[p_N(2h)-p_N(h)]/h. Take N to infinity, then h down to zero. The first bound tends to the right derivative of the limiting convex p; the last is 2p(2h)/(2h)-p(h)/h and has the same limit.
assumptions: pointwise finite pressure limit on an open interval around zero
N limit precedes h down to zero

entries.title: Pressure slope equals the subexponential accessibility threshold
entries.statement: Under the preceding bounded symmetric order-parameter and pointwise pressure-limit assumptions, write A_N=M_N/N and m=p'_+(0). If 0<=a<m, then liminf_N N^{-1}log P(A_N>=a)=0. If m<a<=1, then limsup_N N^{-1}log P(A_N>=a)<0. Conversely, if a>0 and liminf_N N^{-1}log P(A_N>=a)=0, then m>=a. No assertion is made at a=m.
entries.proof_text: For a<m choose small h>0 with p(h)>ha. Splitting the exponential moment at A_N=a gives P(A_N>=a)>=exp(beta N[p_N(h)-h]) [1-exp(beta N[ha-p_N(h)])]. The bracket tends to one; after taking log-rate, let h down to zero, and use that log probabilities have nonpositive rate. For a>m choose h>0 with p(h)/h<a; exponential Markov gives limsup log-rate <=beta[p(h)-ha]<0. Conversely E exp(beta h N A_N)>=exp(beta h N a)P(A_N>=a); zero lower exponential cost implies p(h)>=ha for every h>0, hence m>=a.
assumptions: p_N(h) converges pointwise to finite p(h) on an open interval around zero
strict inequalities a<m or a>m as stated

entries.title: Full-law circular Bragg intensity forces a positive pressure slope
entries.statement: Fix beta>0. Let S_N be complex with |S_N|<=N and a law invariant under multiplication by every unit complex phase. Set M_N=Re S_N and p_N(h)=(beta N)^{-1}log E exp(beta h M_N). Assume p_N converges pointwise near zero to finite p. If liminf_N E|S_N/N|^2>=b^2 for some 0<b<=1, then p'_+(0)>=b. The second moment is under the full zero-field law; a conditional ordered branch does not suffice.
entries.proof_text: Put R_N=|S_N|/N. Fix 0<a<r<b. The moment assumption and 0<=R_N<=1 give P(R_N>=r)>=(b^2-r^2)/[2(1-r^2)] for all sufficiently large N. Circular invariance says that, conditional on any modulus at least r, the probability that Re(S_N/N)>=a is at least arccos(a/r)/pi. Thus P(M_N/N>=a) is bounded below by a positive constant independent of N. The preceding pressure-cost lemma gives p'_+(0)>=a. Let a increase to b through r between a and b.
assumptions: the full zero-field law is invariant under every complex phase rotation
pointwise finite pressure limit near zero
positive liminf full-law second moment b^2

relations.rationale: The probability-cost lemma uses the limiting pressure p and its right derivative m furnished by the bounded order-parameter pressure-limit lemma.
A full-law Bragg second moment plus circular symmetry yields a nonexponentially rare positive real response; the probability-cost lemma then implies the pressure slope bound.

The target seeks a 3D Riesz crystalline Gibbs phase. This conditional bridge would turn an unproved full-law Bragg bound into a pressure cusp, while actual Riesz Bragg intensity, pressure existence, and DLR closure remain open.
